audit_findings.title: FY2025 PAG perimeter is impossible and mismatches the claim denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: The $64.0 million OE anchor excludes PAG, while fully diluted shares and the cash-and-debt bridge are measured after PAG closed on May 5, 2026.
audit_findings.evidence: The Acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions and approvals and is expected to close in the second quarter of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated measurement-date error. The 2025 10-K described PAG as a pending 2026 acquisition, and the June 2026 10-Q confirms the May 5, 2026 closing. Thus FY2025 cannot contain PAG. Combining legacy-VSE cash flow with post-PAG shares and claims prevents the resulting per-share value from representing either legacy VSE or the combined company. PAG contributed $104.5 million of revenue and $6.4 million of net income during the short post-close period, but those figures do not establish its owner earnings.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the valuation on one common date using post-close consolidated OE, all exchangeable PAG shares, TEU settlement shares, offering shares, cash, debt, earn-out and assumed liabilities; alternatively revert every numerator, denominator and bridge item to the pre-PAG perimeter.

audit_findings.title: New PAG financing interest is absent from the owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $54.4 million annualized stated interest on June 30, 2026 principal before swaps, financing-fee amortization and other adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, interest expense must reduce OE; the historical anchor predates the $900.0 million term loan and $66.668 million of amortizing notes.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, indebtedness incurred in connection with the PAG Acquisition, including under the bridge loan and through the issuance of TEUs, may increase the Company’s leverage and debt service obligations and could limit its financial and operational flexibility.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, although the exact forward adjustment remains unresolved. At the filed June 30 rates, $900.0 million at 5.61% plus $66.668 million at 5.93% produces approximately $54.4 million of annualized stated interest, equal to about 85% of the $64.0 million anchor. The $20.556 million FY2025 net-interest expense does not capture the post-PAG capital structure, and H1 2026 net interest is obscured by pre-closing interest income and partial-period financing.
audit_findings.action: Build a post-close interest schedule covering the term loan, amortizing notes, revolver, swaps, commitment fees and financing-fee amortization; purge temporary offering-proceeds interest income and rerun OE and every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The $125 million PAG earn-out is an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $33.850 million recognized fair-value liability; $125.0 million contractual maximum
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement belongs in the equity bridge, while equity settlement belongs in fully diluted shares; neither treatment appears in the valuation.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Purchase Agreement provides for up to $ 125 million in additional contingent earn-out consideration, payable in cash or equity consideration at the Company's sole discretion, based on PAG's 2026 adjusted EBITDA performance.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated omission: the June 2026 balance sheet recognizes a $33.850 million earn-out obligation. That recorded amount equals 3.5% of the $975.0 million base equity value and about $1.05 per current valuation share. The $125.0 million maximum equals 12.8% of base equity value and $3.88 per share, making the claim reasonably capable of materially changing the stated intrinsic value and margin-of-safety threshold.
audit_findings.action: Use the latest filed fair-value liability as the cash-claim base case, test the $125.0 million maximum, and model any equity settlement through incremental shares without also deducting the same amount as cash.

audit_findings.title: The ten-year trend may combine businesses that current shareholders no longer own
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent inclusion of Fleet and Federal and Defense earnings, maintenance capital and working capital could alter the historical OE observations and therefore the fitted $64.0 million anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Prior to the sales of the Federal and Defense and Fleet segments, as discussed below, the Company operated under three reportable operating segments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error. The 2025 filing recasts the periods it presents and states that continuing-operation disclosures exclude discontinued operations, but that does not establish that OE taken from contemporaneous 2016-2022 filings was reconstructed on the same perimeter. The direction is not reliably predictable because removing disposed-business earnings and their reinvestment could change both the level and slope of the log trend.
audit_findings.action: Trace every OE component for 2016-2025 to its source filing and reconstruct all years on a continuing-Aviation-only basis before refitting the trend and rerunning the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Required inventory and working-capital investment may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $56.870 million FY2025 and $115.617 million H1 2026 inventory cash use, net of acquisitions
audit_findings.mechanism: Required normalized investment in inventory, receivables and contract assets reduces OE and makes growth consume cash rather than converting fully into distributable equity cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has made investments in inventory, facilities, and lease commitments to support specific business programs, work requirements, and service offerings.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission itself is unresolved because the supplied record does not show the detailed OE formula or separate maintenance from growth investment. The potential scale is nevertheless demonstrably material: FY2025 inventory cash use was 88.9% of the $64.0 million anchor, and H1 2026 inventory cash use was $115.617 million. These amounts cannot automatically be deducted dollar-for-dollar, but they show that a normalized required-investment adjustment could change the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to operating cash flow by year and estimate normalized maintenance working capital from receivables, contract assets, inventory and operating payables; separate acquisitions and temporary program builds, then rerun each growth scenario with its associated reinvestment requirement.

audit_findings.title: Material inventory valuation depends on subjective recovery assumptions
audit_findings.mechanism: An inadequate obsolescence or net-realizable-value reserve would overstate earnings and historical OE; a later write-down would reduce future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in these assumptions could have a significant impact on the valuation of the inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates estimation risk, not an understated reserve. Inventory was $553.834 million at December 31, 2025 and $867.124 million at June 30, 2026, and the auditor identified slow-moving inventory valuation as a critical audit matter. However, no filed sensitivity or identified misstatement quantifies the possible reserve shortfall, so materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain inventory aging and reserve roll-forwards by location and platform, auditor or management sensitivity ranges, recovery-rate back-testing, exclusive-distribution commitments and subsequent write-downs; rerun OE for any evidenced reserve adjustment.
